newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index gains on blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index gains on blue-chips.

text.p: Strong demand for blue-chip shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) sustained its upward movement on Thursday, bourse officials said.
The index gained 41.03 points to stand at 3514.48. Turnover was posted at 24.420 million shillings on 566,508 shares compared to 96.459 million shillings on 1,617,614 shares.
Dealers said the underlying market sentiment remained bullish, riding high on excitement generated by speculation on the financials' year-end results expected in coming weeks.
They said the bullish tone was sustained despite a drop in the number of shares traded which they blamed on a lack of activity on the special boards.
There was strong demand for the financials, with an emphasis on the big three -- Barclays Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and Kenya Commercial Bank
"There is a big appetite for Kenya Commercial Bank which is just pushing the price up," a bourse official said.
"The gap between Barclays Bank and Kenya Commercial Bank is narrowing, especially now because local investors have joined in the struggle for the share," a senior broker said.
Barclays Bank traded at 117 from 118, while Kenya Commercial Bank edged to close at 98.50 from 96. Standard Chartered Bank gained 2.0 to close at 60.
Uchumi Supermarket gained 3.0 to close at 43 boosted by foreign demand, while Kenya Breweries traded at 62 from 60.50.

"There is a wave of foreign demand which has moved prices upwards in the market," one broker said. "Which is very good because it reflects a growing perception that our market is attractive," he added.

They added that a new entry -- Canada -- had increased the quantity of foreign funds flowing into the Nairobi bourse. Britain and the United States of America are the biggest source of foreign funds in our market.
Unga Group eased to 113 from 118 while British American Tobacco (B.A.T) closed at 64.50 from 60.
